## Good looking leaderboard (all in one):

```{r}
## Loading in necessary packages

library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(ggplot2)
library(stringr)

# Loading data from previously created runner and catcher files
# runner_info contains the runner-side metrics from the previous Rmd file.
# catcher_info contains the catcher-side metrics from the catcher tracking file.
runner_info <- readRDS("runner_info.rds")
catcher_info <- readRDS("catcher_info.rds")
```

# Prepare catcher metrics to use in the existing leaderboard flow

```{r}
# The catcher file already contains the important tracking metrics.
# For the leaderboard maker, we only need:
#   pop_time = catcher catch to receive/tag at second
#   p95_throw_speed_mph = high-end throw speed

# Renamed p95_throw_speed_mph to throw_velo because it is the cleaner project-wide name used in the scoreboard and modeling files.
# Use p95 instead of max throw speed because it is less affected by one-frame tracking spikes, while still representing the upper-end velocity of the throw.

# Create a clean catcher metrics table that can be joined onto the runner data.
# This keeps one row per steal attempt with the catcher metrics needed for the leaderboards and model.

catcher_metrics <- catcher_info %>%
  mutate(
# Convert play_per_game to numeric so it joins correctly with runner_info.   
    play_per_game = as.numeric(play_per_game),
 # Rename the p95 throw speed variable to a shorter project-wide name.
    throw_velo = p95_throw_speed_mph,
# The catcher data does not include catcher names, so this creates a readable label for the catcher leaderboards.
    catcher = "Catcher"
  ) %>%
  filter(
# Keep only throws to second base with reasonable pop time values.
    throw_to_2b,
    pop_time <= 3.5
  ) %>%
  select(
    game_string,
    play_per_game,
    catcher,
    pop_time,
    throw_velo,
    exchange_time,
    flight_time,
    max_throw_speed_mph,
    p95_throw_speed_mph,
    avg_throw_speed_mph,
    arrival_dist_to_2b
  )
```

## Combining runner and catcher info

```{r}
# Combine the runner and catcher metrics into one play-level table.
# game_string + play_per_game identifies each steal attempt.

# Join runner metrics and catcher metrics into one full steal attempt table.
# This creates the main dataset used for both leaderboard graphics and modeling.

steal_attempts_full <- runner_info %>%
  mutate(
  # Make sure play_per_game has the same type in both files before joining.
    play_per_game = as.numeric(play_per_game)
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    catcher_metrics %>%
    select(-any_of("catcher")),
    by = c("game_string", "play_per_game")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
  # Convert runner top speed from feet per second to miles per hour for the scoreboard.
    top_speed_mph = top_speed * 0.681818,
  # Convert jump from feet per second gained to miles per hour gained.
    jump_mph = jump * 0.681818
  )
```


```{r}
## Setting up logic that works for any of the 4 categories

# This table defines the four leaderboard types.
# Each row tells the function which metric to rank, which player column to show, what title/subtitle/unit to use, and whether higher or lower values are better.

metric_settings <- tibble::tribble(
  ~metric_id,           ~metric_col,   ~player_col, ~board_title,              ~board_subtitle,                                      ~unit,          ~higher_is_better, ~priority,
  "runner_top_speed",   "top_speed_mph",   "runner",    "TOP RUNNER SPEEDS",       "Fastest sustained bursts during steal attempts",     "mph",         TRUE,              1,
  "runner_jump",        "jump_mph",        "runner",    "BEST RUNNER JUMPS",       "Most speed gained in the first 0.4 seconds",         "mph gained",  TRUE,              2,
  "catcher_pop_time",   "pop_time",    "catcher",   "FASTEST POP TIMES",       "Quickest catcher throws to second base",         "sec",          FALSE,             3,
  "catcher_throw_velo", "throw_velo",  "catcher",   "HARDEST CATCHER THROWS",  "Highest catcher throw velocities on steal attempts", "mph",          TRUE,              4
)

## Building One Leaderboard

# This function builds one top-10 leaderboard based on the metric settings above.
# It is reused for runner speed, runner jump, catcher pop time, and catcher throw velocity.

build_metric_leaderboard <- function(data, metric_id, metric_col, player_col, board_title, board_subtitle, unit, higher_is_better, priority) {
  
# If a metric column is missing, return an empty table instead of crashing.

  if (!metric_col %in% names(data)) return(tibble())
  
# If the selected player column is missing, fall back to runner.
  if (!player_col %in% names(data)) player_col <- "runner"
 # Keep only real steal outcomes and plays with a valid value for the selected metric.
  metric_data <- data %>%
    filter(
      outcome %in% c("Safe", "Out"),
      !is.na(.data[[metric_col]])
    )
   
# For speed, jump, and throw velocity, higher is better.
# For pop time, lower is better.

  
# Sort the plays differently depending on whether the leaderboard rewards high or low values.
  if (higher_is_better) {
    metric_data <- metric_data %>% arrange(desc(.data[[metric_col]]))
  } else {
    metric_data <- metric_data %>% arrange(.data[[metric_col]])
  }
# Take the top 10 plays and format the columns needed for the scoreboard graphic. 
  metric_data %>%
    slice_head(n = 10) %>%
    mutate(
      rank = row_number(),
      metric_id = metric_id,
      player_id = as.character(.data[[player_col]]),
      board_title = board_title,
      board_subtitle = board_subtitle,
      priority = priority,
  # Shorter game label for scoreboard display
  game_label = str_replace(
  game_string,
  "^y\\d+_d([0-9.]+)_([A-Z]+)_([A-Z]+)$",
  "D\\1: \\2-\\3"),
      metric_value = round(.data[[metric_col]], 2),
      metric_label = paste(metric_value, unit)
    ) %>%
    select(
      metric_id,
      board_title,
      board_subtitle,
      priority,
      rank,
      game_string,
      game_label,
      play_per_game,
      player_id,
      outcome,
      metric_value,
      metric_label
    )
}

# Building one combined trigger table
# A play appears in the table if it ranks top 10 in at least 1 category

# Run the leaderboard function once for each row in metric_settings.
# The result is one combined table of every play that triggered a top-10 leaderboard.

all_leaderboard_triggers <- pmap_dfr(
  metric_settings,
  function(metric_id, metric_col, player_col, board_title, board_subtitle,
    unit, higher_is_better, priority) {
    
    build_metric_leaderboard(
      data = steal_attempts_full,
      metric_id = metric_id,
      metric_col = metric_col,
      player_col = player_col,
      board_title = board_title,
      board_subtitle = board_subtitle,
      unit = unit,
      higher_is_better = higher_is_better,
      priority = priority
    )
  }
)

# Save leaderboard triggers for the graphic maker file.
saveRDS(all_leaderboard_triggers, "all_leaderboard_triggers.rds")

# Scoreboard Graphic

# This function creates the actual top-10 scoreboard graphic.
# It takes one leaderboard table, highlights a specific play if needed, and optionally saves the graphic as a PNG file.

make_scoreboard_leaderboard <- function(board_data,
                                        highlight_game = NULL,
                                        highlight_play = NULL,
                                        output_file = NULL) {
  # If the selected leaderboard has no rows, do not make a graphic.
  if (nrow(board_data) == 0) return(NULL)
  
plot_data <- board_data %>%
  arrange(rank) %>%
  mutate(
  # Create vertical positions for each leaderboard row.
    y = 9.35 - (row_number() - 1) * 0.85,
  # Format the rank as #1, #2, #3, etc.
    rank_label = paste0("#", rank),
    
    # Runner boards show "Player ___".
    # Catcher boards show the catcher/play label directly.
    player_label = if_else(
      str_detect(metric_id, "^catcher"),
      player_id,
      paste0("Player ", player_id)
    ),
  # Mark whether this row is the play that should be highlighted.  
    highlight = .data$game_string == .env$highlight_game &
      .data$play_per_game == .env$highlight_play
  )
 # Build the scoreboard layout with rectangles, text, and row highlights. 
  p <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(y = y)) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
             fill = "#07111F") +
    annotate("rect", xmin = 0, xmax = 100, ymin = 10.95, ymax = 12.4,
             fill = "#12355B") +
    
    annotate("text", x = 50, y = 11.8, label = board_data$board_title[1],
             color = "white", size = 13, fontface = "bold") +
    annotate("text", x = 50, y = 11.2, label = board_data$board_subtitle[1],
             color = "#D8E2F3", size = 5.5) +
  
## Column header annotations    
      
    annotate("text", x = 11, y = 10.45, label = "RANK",
         color = "#AFC4E8", size = 4.5, fontface = "bold") +
    annotate("text", x = 35, y = 10.45, label = "PLAYER",
         color = "#AFC4E8", size = 4.5, fontface = "bold") +
    annotate("text", x = 63, y = 10.45, label = "GAME",
         color = "#AFC4E8", size = 4.5, fontface = "bold") +
    annotate("text", x = 83, y = 10.45, label = "VALUE",
         color = "#AFC4E8", size = 4.5, fontface = "bold") +
  # Draw one row rectangle per leaderboard entry.
  # The highlighted play is shown in gold.   
    geom_rect(
      aes(xmin = 5, xmax = 95, ymin = y - 0.34, ymax = y + 0.34,
          fill = highlight),
      color = "#E8EEF7",
      linewidth = 0.35
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c("FALSE" = "#0B1B2B", "TRUE" = "#D99A25"),
      guide = "none"
    ) +
  # Add the rank, player, game, and metric value text to each row.  
    geom_text(aes(x = 11, label = rank_label),
          color = "white", size = 7, fontface = "bold") +

    geom_text(aes(x = 35, label = player_label),
          color = "white", size = 5.8, fontface = "bold") +

    geom_text(aes(x = 63, label = game_label),
          color = "white", size = 5.3, fontface = "bold") +

    geom_text(aes(x = 83, label = metric_label),
          color = "white", size = 5.8, fontface = "bold") +
    
    annotate("text", x = 50, y = 0.35,
             label = "STOLEN BASE SPOTLIGHT | LIVE TRACKING LEADERBOARD",
             color = "#AFC4E8", size = 4.5, fontface = "bold") +
    
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 100), ylim = c(0, 12.4), expand = FALSE) +
    theme_void()
 # Save the scoreboard image if an output filename is provided. 
  if (!is.null(output_file)) {
    ggsave(output_file, p, width = 16, height = 9, dpi = 150)
  }
  
  p
}
```

# Demo function

```{r}
# This function simulates the live scoreboard workflow.
# Given a specific game and play, it checks whether the play appears in any top-10 leaderboard. If it does, it displays that leaderboard and highlights the selected play.

show_live_scoreboard <- function(game_id, play_id, output_file = NULL) {
  # Find whether the input play triggered any leaderboard.
  triggered <- all_leaderboard_triggers %>%
    filter(
      .data$game_string == .env$game_id,
      .data$play_per_game == .env$play_id
    ) %>%
    arrange(rank, priority)
  # If the play did not make any top-10 leaderboard, do not create a graphic. 
  if (nrow(triggered) == 0) {
    message("No top-10 leaderboard triggered for this play.")
    return(NULL)
  }
 # If the play triggered a leaderboard, select the first/best leaderboard to show. 
  board_to_show <- all_leaderboard_triggers %>%
    filter(metric_id == triggered$metric_id[1]) %>%
    arrange(rank)
# Create the scoreboard graphic and highlight the input play.  
  make_scoreboard_leaderboard(
    board_data = board_to_show,
    highlight_game = game_id,
    highlight_play = play_id,
    output_file = output_file
  )
}
```

## Setup data for modeling:

```{r}
# Create the clean modeling dataset used by the stolen base modeling file.
# This takes the full runner/catcher table and creates model-friendly outcome columns.

modeling_data <- steal_attempts_full %>%
  mutate(
    # Keep the original outcome column for reference.
    outcome_raw = outcome,
     # Standardize the outcome text so Safe and caught stealing plays can be identified consistently.
    outcome_clean = str_to_lower(str_trim(as.character(outcome))),
    # Clean outcome into a model-friendly version.
    outcome_model = case_when(
      outcome_clean == "safe" ~ "Safe",
      str_detect(outcome_clean, "caught") ~ "Out",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    
    # Binary version for ROC/AUC and threshold selection.
    safe_binary = if_else(outcome_model == "Safe", 1, 0),
    
    # Factor version for classification models like random forest.
    outcome_factor = factor(outcome_model, levels = c("Out", "Safe"))
  ) %>%
  filter(
  # Keep only plays with valid outcomes and all four model input metrics.
    outcome_model %in% c("Safe", "Out"),
    !is.na(top_speed_mph),
    !is.na(jump),
    !is.na(pop_time),
    !is.na(throw_velo)
  ) %>%
  select(
    game_string,
    play_per_game,
    runner,
    catcher,
    outcome_raw,
    outcome_model,
    safe_binary,
    outcome_factor,
    top_speed,
    top_speed_mph,
    jump,
    pop_time,
    throw_velo,
    exchange_time,
    flight_time,
    arrival_dist_to_2b
  )

# Save the modeling dataset so the modeling file can load it directly.
saveRDS(modeling_data, "steal_modeling_data.rds")
```
